assumptions.description: The task is an equal-stratum analytical design: each sex crossed with integer age bands 25-39,40-54,55-69,70-79 has exactly375 rows. Within each cell age is uniform over integers, fictional independent individuals conditional on fixed stratum assignments. Not national prevalence weights.

A qualified Lifelines source law uses independent age Uniform(55.5-sqrt(3)*9.9,55.5+sqrt(3)*9.9) and female Bernoulli(0.597). It reproduces admitted marginal moments but not the actual age distribution, GWAS recruitment or Table2 row-specific cases. Table1 and Table2 are treated as representing the same law as an unverified completion assumption.

A qualified Pani NHANES population law uses independent integer age Uniform{25,...,84} and female Bernoulli(0.5), with the same conditional equations as the target and Lifelines law. The upper age84 is an explicit technical source-completion assumption, not an admitted source cutoff. In particular the reported >=70 band is approximated by70-84. Uniform age weights and sex balance are assumed population probabilities, not source survey weights or counts.

BMI and glucose conditional means have assumed age slopes0.04 kg/m^2/year and0.12 mg/dL/year and female-minus-male shifts0.4 kg/m^2 and-2 mg/dL. Residual correlation0.30 is an unsupported completion choice; it is not identified by the two Jansen projections. Demographic independence and zero other latent cross-covariances are structural assumptions, not absence-of-evidence facts.

Three independent standardized symmetric Beta(3,3) variables drive BMI, glucose and HbA1c residuals. Each has mean0, variance1 and support[-sqrt(7),sqrt(7)]. This is an assumed bounded, continuous, symmetric residual law; its support is a modeling limitation, not a population cutoff. No clipping or rejection is performed.

Conditional HbA1c expectation is additive and linear in age, female, BMI and glucose, with constant independent residual variance and no interactions. Direct female coefficient0 is an explicit simplifying assumption. This conditional equation is an associational law, not a causal structural claim.

Jansen locations, variation and separate BMI/glucose projections and the Pani adjusted age association are transported to one common conditional law. Source ancestry, age distributions, source row exclusions, plasma versus target serum glucose, assays, fasting duration, pregnancy routing, anemia and medication differences are unverified. Common coefficients across sources and the task are assumptions; no target statistic was available.

The law describes an already eligible analytical population; non-diabetes diagnosis,8-12-hour fast, standing anthropometry consistency and routed pregnancy/lactation exclusions are membership premises, not simulated measured flags. It includes no verified anemia or medication exclusion. All generated glucose is positive and<126 by derived support, not an HbA1c diagnostic screen.

External estimates are fixed plug-in anchors. The unknown-level Jansen printed interval bounds and Pani P value do not yield SEs. Pani age-band SEs quantify source survey estimate uncertainty, not individual dispersion. Seeds change individual residual realizations, not external-estimate, structural or transport uncertainty.

Jansen Table1 and Table2 belong to Lifelines and are not independent studies. Original and converted versions are single quantities. Pani slope and age-band means are one NHANES source, potentially overlapping other NHANES reports; no such other report is used. Pani FOS results are not pooled. No cross-study uncertainty independence is claimed.

Target output cannot reconstruct either source population. Every whole-cohort source-comparison recipe is unavailable. Separate analytic projections evaluate the explicit approximate source law; these do not certify survey replay or target validity.

design.derivation: Exact supplied task quotas; within-cell law and identifier prefix are implementation choices.

units.derivation: Exact task output units and coding.

latent.derivation: Beta shape3 is a completion assumption; standardization is Z=(2U-1)*sqrt(2*shape+1).

centers.derivation: Use reported percent HbA1c mean5.6, not both it and converted IFCC mean as separate constraints. Centers are source anchors, not forced target margins.

covariate_effects.derivation: Author-selected covariate slopes, sex shifts and residual correlation; not inferred from absence of cross-covariances.

source_marginal_sds.derivation: Use reported percent SD0.3, not the alternative rounded IFCC SD as an independent constraint.

source_projection_constraints.derivation: Each original/converted pair is one quantity. Jansen gives two different age/sex-adjusted population projections, and Pani gives an adjusted age projection.

response.derivation: Solve bB=(tB-rho*sG/sB*tG)/(1-rho^2), bG=(tG-rho*sB/sG*tB)/(1-rho^2); bA=0.01, bF=0. These are not direct assignments of both Jansen projections to joint coefficients.

residual_scales.derivation: Subtract age/sex explained variance from BMI/glucose marginal variances; subtract all linear predictor variance from HbA1c variance. Exact formulas and positive remainders retained in analytic_calculations.py and analytic_results.json.

source_contexts.derivation: Source-context demographic laws are separately specified. Pani support25-84 and probabilities are assumptions, not Jansen demographics or target equal-stratum proportions.

measurement_conversion.derivation: Fixed admitted unit conversions; additive offset only for HbA1c levels, never slopes/SD. No eAG relation is used.
